subject: chemistry
question_text: Explain the hybridization involved in the SF₆ molecule.

verification.note: Chapter 3 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

steps.label: sp³d² hybridisation of S
lines: In SF₆ the central atom S undergoes sp³d²
One 3s, three 3p and two 3d orbitals mix to
give six identical sp³d² hybrid orbitals.
steps.why: Sulphur has only two unpaired electrons in the ground state, but SF₆ needs six bonds. Two excitations give six half-filled orbitals, which mix into six sp³d² hybrids.
common_mistakes: Writing sp³d instead of sp³d². Six bonds need six hybrids, so TWO d orbitals join.
Writing first excited state. Six unpaired electrons need the SECOND excited state of sulphur.
steps.memory_tip: Count the bonds first: six bonds means six hybrids, so s + three p + two d.
steps.margin_note: The words second excited state matter here — one excitation gives only four unpaired electrons.

steps.label: Overlap with fluorine
lines: Each half-filled sp³d² hybrid orbital of S
steps.why: Six hybrids on S meet six half-filled 2p orbitals, one from each F atom, so exactly six axial overlaps and six σ bonds form.
common_mistakes: Writing 3p for fluorine. Fluorine's half-filled orbital is a 2p orbital.
Calling the bonds π. Axial overlap gives σ bonds.
steps.memory_tip: Each F brings one half-filled 2p orbital; each S hybrid meets one of them.
steps.margin_note: Name the bond type in full: σ(sp³d²–p).

steps.label: The diagram
steps.why: The shape mark needs the drawn arrangement: four bonds in a plane and two on the vertical axis, all at 90°. The dashed bond shows one F behind the plane of the page.
common_mistakes: Drawing SF₆ as a hexagon of six F atoms around S in one plane. The shape is octahedral, not planar.
Leaving the 90° label off the diagram.
steps.memory_tip: Up, down, left, right, front, back — six directions at right angles, one F on each.
steps.margin_note: A neat small diagram is enough. Label one 90° angle.

steps.label: Shape and bond angle
lines: All six S−F bonds are equivalent, and
every adjacent pair of bonds is at 90°.
steps.why: Unlike PCl₅, all six positions of an octahedron are equivalent, so one bond angle describes the whole molecule.
common_mistakes: Writing 60° because a hexagon has 60° angles. The shape is a three-dimensional octahedron with 90° angles.
steps.memory_tip: Six directions at right angles: every neighbouring pair is 90°.
steps.margin_note: One shape name, one angle — this line closes the answer.

insider_note: The contrast with PCl₅ is what examiners probe: SF₆ needs the SECOND excited state and gives one single bond angle, 90°, because all six positions are equivalent.
